Now by Theorem III, Art. 21,
$$\iint \frac{d \Psi}{d \nu} d s=-\iiint \nabla^{2} \Psi d x d y d z$$
since $d \nu$ is here measured outwards from the sphere, and this

cally greater than
$$\frac{4}{3} \pi \alpha^{2} e\left(\nabla^{2} \Psi\right)_{\theta},$$
and is therefore of the order $a^{2}$, and may be neglected when "
vanishes.
But the surface-integral for the sphere on the other side of
the equation, namely,
does not vanish, for
$$\begin{gathered}
\iint \Psi \frac{d \Phi}{d \nu} d s^{\prime} \\
\iint \frac{d \Phi}{d \nu} d s^{\prime}=-4 \pi e
\end{gathered}$$
$d \nu$ being measured outwards from the sphere, and if $\Psi_{0}$ be the
value of $\Psi$ at the point $P$,
